answer.answer: Paragraph 14 most naturally attaches “upon SFC’s request” to demonstration, leaving confirmation unqualified by that trigger. Both concern management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity; demonstration expressly carries the standard of the SFC’s satisfaction. Footnote 5 specifies minimum content for confirmation and demonstration: compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence. Its omission of a request condition creates a supported rival reading that demonstration is standing. Reading the footnote as elaborating paragraph 14 instead preserves the request trigger. Without a request, confirmation remains applicable on these readings; demonstration is untriggered under the main-text and integrated readings, but remains applicable under the standing-footnote reading. None of this establishes fulfillment. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on an applicable SFC request.

claims.proposition: Paragraph 14 separates unqualified confirmation from request-triggered demonstration of the same three subjects.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

claims.inference: Text and grammatical deduction: the inserted request phrase immediately qualifies “demonstrate”; the common objects follow both verbs. “To the SFC’s satisfaction” expressly qualifies demonstration. Applying that same acceptance standard independently to confirmation would require further interpretation.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the entity, product, activity and assessment period, including relevant conditions or modifications.
Any applicable requirements governing the timing, form and sufficiency of confirmation.

claims.proposition: Footnote 5 supplies minimum substantive content for confirmation and demonstration, but leaves a trigger tension with paragraph 14.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.
upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction

claims.inference: Text: the footnote addresses both verbs and states minimum content. The high-confidence wording attaches most directly to the assertion about smart-contract vulnerabilities and security flaws; extending it to every aspect of paragraphs 10–13 is not expressly established. Judgment: reading this content together with paragraph 14 preserves both high confidence concerning smart contracts and the SFC-satisfaction standard for demonstration.
missing_premises: An authoritative resolution of whether the footnote retains or independently displaces the main-text request trigger.
An applicable evidential meaning of “high level of confidence” and the SFC’s satisfaction.
Evidence supporting compliance and smart-contract integrity.

claims.proposition: No request has different consequences under the rival demonstration readings, but supplies no conclusion of compliance.

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate
Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC

Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

claims.inference: Conditional deduction: assuming no applicable request was made, the demonstration trigger is unsatisfied under readings A and C. Under reading B, the footnote's unqualified demonstration language remains operative. Absence of a request does not remove confirmation or the underlying substantive requirements, and does not prove that any applicable requirement has been fulfilled.
missing_premises: Reliable evidence of whether an SFC request covers the relevant activity and period; an unknown request status is not absence.
Resolution of the competing trigger readings.
Actual confirmation, controls, records and other evidence assessed against applicable standards.

claims.proposition: Paragraphs 15 and 16 concern distinct requested deliverables rather than confirmation or demonstration alone.

support.quote: Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

claims.inference: Text and deduction: paragraph 15 requires obtaining third-party audit or verification concerning the three identified subjects; paragraph 16 requires obtaining a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. Each has its own request condition. A request for demonstration does not automatically request either additional deliverable, although one SFC communication could expressly request several. Neither paragraph itself specifies footnote 5’s high-confidence standard for its deliverable.
missing_premises: The content and scope of any SFC request under each paragraph.
Applicable audit, verification or legal-opinion scope and sufficiency criteria.
Evidence that the requested deliverable was obtained and meets those criteria.

rival_readings: A — Main-text reading: demonstration is requested and must satisfy the SFC on paragraph 14’s three subjects; the precise attachment of footnote 5’s content and standard remains open.

B — Standing-footnote reading: the unqualified “confirm and demonstrate” supports demonstration even without a request, with the stated minimum content. This reading must address the contrary express main-text trigger; omission alone does not establish priority.

C — Integrated reading: footnote 5 elaborates the minimum content of confirmation and requested demonstration while paragraph 14 retains the demonstration trigger and SFC-satisfaction standard. This reconciles the provisions without deleting the express trigger, but is an interpretive judgment rather than an established authoritative resolution.
unresolved: The supplied material does not authoritatively resolve the main-text/footnote trigger tension.
Confirmation timing and procedure, the evidence constituting high confidence, and the criteria for SFC satisfaction are not established here.
Entity-specific applicability, requests and fulfillment facts are absent.
The provisions use “should”; formal rule labels, graph acceptance and serialization results do not establish legal force, interpretive priority or compliance.
